title: the-hollow-measures-the-repaired-build
intention: The hollow measures the build that stands after a FIXME repair: a back-edge into FIXME does not move the anchor past the build it repairs, a writes_to directory is measured file by file, and a moved file identical at the anchor reads unwritten, never hollow.
why: efb670ff1dd8 is built, repaired under FIXME 1, and its proof is sealed green, but it cannot cross to PROVED: the hollow (2026-10-02, HEAD d95e8cbe) reverted to the repair's parent, read liveness.py hollow on an unchanged world, skipped the ground_loop/ directory holding the repair, and blamed the chart for four files the build did write. A reading that measures the wrong window sends the next mind to fix a chart and a proof that are right (Law 7).
traces_to: Law 7 (a record of truth may not collapse an error into the wrong shape: 'hollow' on an unchanged file and 'unwritten' on files the build wrote both blame the wrong leg) and Law 8 (the hollow keeps a hollow build out of proven-space; it must measure the build that stands); 06f0445e7a63 (the hollow anchors before the build that stands)
how: Three defects in cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py, measured on efb670ff1dd8's hollow 2026-10-02. (1) build_anchor bounds the build-commit search by the latest back-edge out of BUILDME or PROVEME that has a build commit after it. efb's only back-edge is PROVEME->FIXME (2026-10-02T14:17), and its repair c2d2fedf follows, so the anchor became c2d2fedf^ = 5fa2114e and the original build 4313a42d fell outside the window. A FIXME crossing repairs the standing build, it does not replace it: a back-edge whose `to` is FIXME does not bound. Back-edges to BUILDME or TICKETME (the 06f0445e7a63 rebuild cases, 68f563403c8f and c691e19d5464) bound exactly as now. (2) measure()'s file loop tests (wt / rel).is_file(), so a writes_to entry naming a directory falls through to moved_to and is skipped as 'not present at HEAD and no recorded successor'. A directory entry expands, after the anchor is chosen, to `git diff --name-only <anchor> HEAD -- <dir>`, each file then classified and measured as any other; a directory with no file changed since the anchor is skipped as 'a directory the build left unchanged'. (3) For a moved file, `how` gains the suffix '; moved from <source>, restored there' before the `how == "unchanged"` test, so a successor byte-identical at the anchor whose source was absent there too never reads UNWRIT; the suite runs on an unchanged world and the file reads HOLLOW. The test compares the successor's own result, and the source half counts as a change only when it wrote or removed a file.
falsifier: RED if after the build: (1) in a scratch repo with a build commit, a PROVEME->FIXME back-edge and a repair commit after it, build_anchor anchors at the repair's parent instead of the build's parent; (2) a writes_to entry naming a directory present at HEAD is skipped instead of measured file by file over the files the ticket's own build commits changed under it since the anchor, or a file another ticket's commit changed there is measured as this build; (3) a moved file whose successor is byte-identical at the anchor and whose source is absent there reads HOLLOW instead of UNWRIT; (4) the existing anchor proof test_hollow_anchors_before_the_build_that_stands.py or test_hollow.py turns red; (5) a file the build added is reverted by removal and leaves its parent directory behind, empty, where the anchor had no such directory — a clean checkout of the anchor has none. WRONG INTENT if Akien answers that a FIXME repair is a rebuild whose hollow measures only the repair. Horizon: efb670ff1dd8's hollow sealed after this build.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [FIXME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> PROVED
watchme: none, because the falsifier is read by `bin/cairn test --hollow efb670ff1dd8` (bin/cmd/test) at efb670ff1dd8's PROVED attempt, and the reading lands as evidence.hollow on cairn/tools/bus_client/validations/test_the_wiring_needs_no_loop.json, an existing record; nothing further to learn after that one reading.
children: none, because the change is one filter, one helper and one comparison inside hollow.py.
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Which lines? cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py build_anchor's `backs` list comprehension gains `and c.get('to') != 'FIXME'` with a comment naming efb670ff1dd8; measure() gains a helper `_expand_dirs(files, commit, repo_root, wt) -> list[str]` that replaces each entry whose (repo_root / rel).is_dir() with the sorted output of `git diff --name-only <commit> HEAD -- <rel>` (keeping file entries in place, deduped, order kept), and records a skip {'file': rel, 'why': 'a directory the build left unchanged'} when the diff is empty; the move branch tests `how == 'unchanged'` on the successor's result and treats the source half as a no-op when the source is absent at the anchor and absent in the worktree. (2) What proves it? a new proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_measures_the_repaired_build.py over scratch git repos (the fixture pattern of test_hollow_anchors_before_the_build_that_stands.py): teeth a_fixme_back_edge_does_not_bound_the_anchor, a_writes_to_directory_is_measured_per_file, an_unchanged_move_reads_unwritten. (3) The live reading: bin/cairn test --hollow efb670ff1dd8 --seal after the build.

decisions.text: The builder does NOT write the proof. cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_measures_the_repaired_build.py was committed red at 0f82875b (1 of 4 green at HEAD: teeth a_fixme_back_edge_does_not_bound_the_anchor, a_writes_to_directory_is_measured_per_file and an_unchanged_move_reads_unwritten red; the_anchor_and_hollow_proofs_stay_green green). Its PROVES keys 1-4 follow the falsifier's numbered clauses. The builder runs it and edits it not at all; the build is done when it exits 0.

In cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py build_anchor, the list comprehension that builds `backs` (it filters crossings_for(tid, roots) to direction in ('back', 'backward'), from in ('BUILDME', 'PROVEME') and a truthy at) gains one more condition, `and c.get("to") != "FIXME"`. Directly above the comprehension add a comment of at most four lines: a back-edge INTO FIXME repairs the standing build and does not replace it, so it bounds nothing (ticket e08c996f939c, measured on efb670ff1dd8, whose PROVEME->FIXME back-edge anchored the hollow at the repair's parent). Back-edges to BUILDME or TICKETME are untouched. Nothing else in build_anchor changes, and its docstring's RULE paragraph gains one sentence saying the same.
decisions.step: a FIXME back-edge does not bound

decisions.text: In cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py, add a module function just above def measure: `def _expand_dirs(files: list[str], commit: str, repo_root: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[dict]]`. For each entry in order: if (Path(repo_root) / rel).is_dir() is False, keep it as is. If it is a directory, run `git -C <repo_root> diff --name-only <commit> HEAD -- <rel>` through the existing helper _git_ok(repo_root, 'diff', '--name-only', commit, 'HEAD', '--', rel) and put each non-empty output line in place of the entry; when the output is empty, put nothing in its place and append {'file': rel, 'why': 'a directory the build left unchanged since the anchor'} to the second list. The first list is deduped keeping first occurrence. In measure(), on the line right after `commit, at = anchor["commit"], anchor["buildme_at"]`, add `files, dir_skips = _expand_dirs(files, commit, repo_root)`. Further down, the line `skipped: list[dict] = []` becomes `skipped: list[dict] = list(dir_skips)`, followed by `for s in dir_skips: log(f"  skip   {s['file']}  ({s['why']})")`. build_anchor is still called with the unexpanded list (git log -- <dir> already matches it).
decisions.step: a writes_to directory expands per file

decisions.text: In cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py measure()'s file loop, the move branch now reads: `how = _revert(wt, commit, rel, repo_root=repo_root)`; then `if source is not None:` compute `src_was = (wt / source).exists()` BEFORE calling `src_how = _revert(wt, commit, source, repo_root=repo_root)`; the source half is a no-op when src_how == 'unchanged', or when src_how starts with 'removed' and src_was is False. If how == 'unchanged' and the source half is a no-op, leave `how` as 'unchanged' (so the existing `if how == "unchanged":` branch reads it UNWRIT and _restore runs); otherwise set `how = f"{how}; moved from {source}, restored there"` exactly as today. In the UNWRIT branch, when source is not None and (wt / source).exists() and src_was is False, unlink it, the same clean-up the run branch's finally already does. The comment above the move branch gains one line naming e08c996f939c: the suffix used to be added before the unchanged test, so a no-op move read HOLLOW.

After the three edits in cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py, run `python3 cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_measures_the_repaired_build.py`; it exits 0 with 4 of 4 teeth green (tooth 4 runs test_hollow_anchors_before_the_build_that_stands.py and test_hollow.py inside it and takes several minutes; run it in the background). Then commit only cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py, with the subject line 'e08c996f939c: build — the hollow measures the repaired build: a FIXME back-edge bounds nothing, a directory expands, an unchanged move reads unwritten' and the session's attribution trailer after a blank line.

NOT builder steps: sealing the proof (bin/cairn test --seal), the PROVEME crossing, `bin/cairn test --hollow e08c996f939c --seal`, and re-running `bin/cairn test --hollow efb670ff1dd8 --seal` are CC's acts after the build commit. The builder stops at the build commit.

decisions.text: Measured at HEAD 0f82875b, cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py build_anchor (line 223) reads, at lines 245-247: `backs = [c for c in crossings_for(tid, roots)` / `if c.get("direction") in ("back", "backward")` / `and c.get("from") in ("BUILDME", "PROVEME") and c.get("at")]`. The edit appends ` and c.get("to") != "FIXME"` inside that final condition, before the closing bracket, and puts a comment of at most four lines directly above `backs =`: a back-edge INTO FIXME repairs the standing build and does not replace it, so it bounds nothing (ticket e08c996f939c, measured on efb670ff1dd8). The docstring has a paragraph opening 'THE RULE.' whose last sentence (line 233) ends 'a back-edge with no build after it is a retreat-and-recross and bounds nothing.'; right after that sentence, inside the same paragraph, add: 'A back-edge INTO FIXME bounds nothing either: a repair stands on the build it repairs (ticket e08c996f939c).' Nothing else in build_anchor changes.
decisions.step: where the FIXME filter and its docstring sentence go

decisions.text: Measured at HEAD 0f82875b, cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py measure()'s file loop (from line 701) holds, at lines 716-733: `how = _revert(wt, commit, rel, repo_root=repo_root)`; then `if source is not None:` with a comment 'THE COUNTERFACTUAL OF A MOVE IS BOTH HALVES...' and the two lines `_revert(wt, commit, source, repo_root=repo_root)` and `how = f"{how}; moved from {source}, restored there"`; then `if how == "unchanged":` appending rel to unchanged, calling _restore(wt, rel), logging '  UNWRIT ...' and `continue`; then `try: after, after_ran, _ = run_all()` with `finally: _restore(wt, rel)` and `if source is not None and (wt / source).exists(): (wt / source).unlink()`. The new shape: before the `if source is not None:` block put `src_noop = True`. Inside that block, first `src_was = (wt / source).exists()`, then `src_how = _revert(wt, commit, source, repo_root=repo_root)`, then `src_noop = src_how == "unchanged" or (src_how.startswith("removed") and not src_was)`, then `if not (how == "unchanged" and src_noop): how = f"{how}; moved from {source}, restored there"`. Keep the existing comment and add one line to it: 'A no-op on both halves stays "unchanged" and reads UNWRIT (ticket e08c996f939c: the suffix used to be added first, so a no-op move read HOLLOW).' Inside the `if how == "unchanged":` branch, right after _restore(wt, rel), add `if source is not None and not src_was and (wt / source).exists(): (wt / source).unlink()` so the worktree is left as the run branch's finally leaves it. The try/finally is untouched.
decisions.step: the move branch as it stands and as it becomes

decisions.text: The build commit's message is the subject line 'e08c996f939c: build — the hollow measures the repaired build: a FIXME back-edge bounds nothing, a directory expands, an unchanged move reads unwritten', then one blank line, then exactly these two trailer lines: 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>' and 'Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JrhBQALF5qFBEVqQJUsXUu'. No Signed-off-by line.

In cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py, the function _expand_dirs(files, commit, repo_root) keeps its signature and return shape, but a directory entry no longer expands to every file changed between the anchor and HEAD. It expands to the files changed under that directory by the commits after the anchor whose message names the ticket id. To do that, _expand_dirs gains a keyword parameter tid: str, and its git call becomes _git_ok(repo_root, 'log', '--format=', '--name-only', '-F', f'--grep={tid}', f'{commit}..HEAD', '--', rel); each non-empty output line is a file path (dedupe, keep first occurrence, and keep only paths that exist as files at (Path(repo_root) / path)). When nothing is left the directory is skipped with why 'a directory no build commit of this ticket changed since the anchor'. The call in measure() becomes files, dir_skips = _expand_dirs(files, commit, repo_root, tid=tid). The docstring gains one sentence: files another ticket's commit changed after the anchor are not this build and are never measured (FIXME 1, measured 2026-10-02 on efb670ff1dd8: ground_loop/__main__.py, cli.py, discovery.py and intention+why.json, edited by other tickets, read HOLLOW). The proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_measures_the_repaired_build.py already carries the red tooth (its tooth a_writes_to_directory_is_measured_per_file asserts pkg/other.py, changed by an unrelated commit after the build, is neither measured nor hollow); the builder does not edit it. Run that proof until it exits 0 with 4 of 4 teeth green, then commit only hollow.py with the subject 'e08c996f939c: FIXME 1 — a directory expands to the files the ticket's own build commits changed' followed by a blank line and the two lines 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>' and 'Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JrhBQALF5qFBEVqQJUsXUu'.

In cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py, _revert's removal branch (the 'if probe.returncode != 0:' block, which today unlinks target if it exists and returns 'removed (absent before the build)') gains, after the unlink and before the return, a walk up from target.parent toward the worktree root: for each directory d strictly inside the worktree, stop if d is not a directory, or os.listdir(d) is non-empty, or git -C repo_root cat-file -e '{commit}:{d relative to worktree, as posix}' returns 0 (the anchor had that directory); otherwise d.rmdir() and continue with d.parent. The worktree root itself is never removed. The return string stays 'removed (absent before the build)'. _restore needs no change: 'git checkout -- rel' recreates parent directories. Tooth 5 (test_a_removed_file_takes_its_empty_directory_with_it) is the arbiter; teeth 1-4 must stay green. This lands in the same build commit as D10, subject 'e08c996f939c: FIXME 1+2 — a directory expands to the ticket's own build files; a removed file takes its empty directory with it'; D10's own subject line is superseded by this one.
decisions.step: FIXME 2 — the removal branch prunes the directories it emptied

fixme.missing: _expand_dirs expands a writes_to directory to `git diff --name-only <anchor> HEAD -- <dir>`, which includes files OTHER tickets changed after the anchor. Measured 2026-10-02 on efb670ff1dd8's hollow (HEAD f670e2fb, anchor 1923f254): ground_loop/__main__.py and cli.py (59ade57ef280, 89bfb8fb), discovery.py (the 09-30 restatement, 507a15ad) and intention+why.json (56d1aff4455e and others) read HOLLOW although no efb670ff1dd8 commit touched them — the proof blamed for another hand's edit (Law 7). A directory must expand only to the files the ticket's own build commits (those naming the ticket id after the anchor) changed under it; tooth 2's fixture gains an unrelated commit after the build that the reading must not measure.

_revert removes a file absent at the anchor but leaves its parent directories, now empty, in the worktree. Measured 2026-10-02 on efb670ff1dd8: reverting ground_loop/probes/__init__.py (added by c2d2fedf) left an empty probes/ folder, discovery still registered ground_loop by that folder, and tooth 3 stayed green — so the file read HOLLOW. With the empty folder removed as well, tooth 3 reds (LookupError: no shim answers to 'ground_loop'), measured in a scratch worktree at HEAD f670e2fb. The counterfactual of 'the build had not happened' is a clean checkout of the anchor, which has no empty directory.
